- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% below peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% for next 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above 80, adjust downward by 1–3% per day if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period — reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 2–4% if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.2), model tends to lag — add 1–2% lagged sentiment adjustment to forecast.
